title: Get started

Choose how to connect to Console, then try an analysis.
No Console configuration file is required.

## Choose how to connect {#connect-your-client}

<span id="codex-and-claude-code"></span> <span id="other-mcp-clients"></span> <span id="r-and-python-packages"></span>

| Use Console with…                    | Start here                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A coding agent or another MCP client | [MCP client setup](CLIENTS.md) covers Codex, Claude Code, and manual MCP settings.         |
| R                                    | [Use Console from R](R.md) adds a Console tool to an ellmer chat.                          |
| Python                               | [Use Console from Python](PYTHON.md) covers direct calls and model framework integrations. |

All three use the same persistent workbench for R, Python, and SQL.
Once connected, continue with the analysis below or explore the [guides](README.md).

## Install

[Installation](INSTALLATION.md) covers uv, supported platforms, and the runtimes your agent can use.
The R and Python guides above also cover installing their client packages.

<span id="build-from-source"></span>

To install the development version, follow [Build from source](BUILD_FROM_SOURCE.md).

## Try an analysis

With R installed, ask your agent:

> Use MCP Console to tell me something interesting about the Palmer Penguins dataset.
> Load the data from `palmerpenguins` in R and summarize it by species with SQL.
> Fit a model in R to predict body mass from flipper length, and plot the data and fitted model in Python.
> Keep the data and model for follow-up.

Then ask:

> Which observations does the model fit poorly?
> Show a plot and the path to the recorded session.

See [Sessions and languages](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md) for an example of how your agent can combine languages and build on earlier work.

## Choose permissions

For Codex registered through [client setup](CLIENTS.md#codex-and-claude-code), Console defaults to the client's sandbox permissions; configuration files can select another profile.
Without inheritance or a configured profile, the default sandbox permits file reads and private temporary writes, but not ordinary workspace writes or direct network access.
**It does not protect readable secrets.**

### Allow project writes {#allow-project-writes}

To let the agent save files in one project, create Console configuration in the directory where the client launches it:

```sh
uvx mcp-console config init
```

This creates `.agents/console/config.yaml` with `sandbox.profile: workspace`.
Restart the client to load the settings.
The `workspace` profile allows writes in Console's launch directory except in sensitive locations such as `.agents` and `.git`.
File reads remain allowed and direct network access remains restricted.

The command-line reference covers [workspace writes across projects](CLI.md#allow-workspace-writes-across-projects) and [grants for individual directories](CLI.md#grant-writes-to-one-directory).
See [Sandbox permissions](SANDBOX_CONFIGURATION.md) for the permission rules.

Console loads project configuration automatically, and it can select executables or widen permissions.
Review and authorize it before launching Console in an unfamiliar project; `--no-project-config` skips that layer.

For interpreter selection and package setup, see [Interpreters and startup](RUNTIME_CONFIGURATION.md) and [Packages and environments](REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Keep the session

Console records transcripts and artifacts locally.
[Recordings and reports](RECORDING.md) explains where to find them and how to turn a reviewed copy into a report.

Recordings are not checkpoints.
They contain input and output without redaction and are not automatically deleted.
